passage:
“Jasleen, give Nani a kiss goodnight,” said Rajni. Jasleen leaned over, lips pushed into a small round pucker, and pressed them against the phone screen.
“Mmmwah!” said Nani from the phone.
“Now shoes,” said Rajni. Jasleen sat down and sucked her lips in, tongue out a little, pulling at a strap.
“You're working hard.”
Then the doorbell rang and Jasleen stretched her lips wide and squealed, “Papa!”

qa.q: What did Jasleen press her puckered lips against?
qa.a: The phone screen, to kiss Nani goodnight.

qa.q: What might Jasleen's stretched lips and squeal at the doorbell mean, and what alternative is there?
qa.a: They most likely show excitement that Papa is home. They might also just be a loud reaction to the doorbell sound.

qa.q: What could Rajni do to build on this play?
qa.a: Rajni could name each feeling as it happens, like “You're excited!”, and copy the kiss or the squeal back playfully.

qa.q: How might Nani feel receiving a kiss through the phone?
qa.a: She probably feels loved and delighted that her granddaughter did it on her own, even from far away.

grounding: A toddler puckers for a kiss, sucks in her lips in concentration and stretches them in an excited squeal.

passage: Playgroup note, Wednesday. Pallavi, two, puckered her lips and gave her doll a loud kiss during the tea-party game. Later, threading big wooden beads, she pulled her lips tightly in and held them there until the bead went on. When rain began on the roof, she stretched her mouth wide and squealed with her arms flapping. Same little mouth, three different meanings. I will keep watching what she is doing each time before guessing. 🙂 Himani

qa.q: What was Pallavi doing when she sucked her lips in?
qa.a: She was threading big wooden beads.

qa.q: What did Pallavi's wide mouth and squeal at the rain show she was feeling?
qa.a: It probably shows excitement, since her arms flapped as well. It could also be a reaction to the sudden sound of rain on the roof.

qa.q: What is Himani's plan for reading Pallavi's mouth shapes?
qa.a: Himani will look at what Pallavi is doing each time before guessing, because the same lip movement can mean different things.

qa.q: How might Pallavi's mother feel hearing this?
qa.a: She may enjoy hearing her daughter is exploring so many ways to show feelings, and may notice them herself at home.

grounding: A toddler puckers, tightens and stretches her lips in different contexts, each with a different meaning.
